# SHARED PROJECTED-COST RELATION CORPUS (task 1.5-h).
#
# A RELATION, NOT A CEILING, and the distinction decides everything about the shape. The
# numbers here are NOT frozen ABI constants: the maxima are carried by the record's OWN
# production capability, so each comparison is between two values that travel together. A
# manifest of literals would therefore be meaningless -- what is frozen is the SHAPE of the
# comparison, and that is what these rows pin.
#
# THREE CONJUNCTS, EACH INDEPENDENTLY REMOVABLE. `validateProductionCapability` refuses when the
# cost model versions DIFFER, or when either projected quantity EXCEEDS its capability-carried maximum.
# Deleting any one leaves the other two refusing their own inputs, so a single row cannot
# stand in for the group.
#
# INCLUSIVITY IS HALF OF EACH QUANTITY ROW. "Over is refused" alone permits an implementation
# to tighten `>` into `>=` and refuse a record projecting EXACTLY its capability-carried maximum -- a
# conforming producer's record, refused. Each quantity therefore carries an AT-MAXIMUM
# acceptance as well.
#
# PRE-SIGNATURE, AND THE ROWS SAY SO. The comparison runs inside `ValidateRecord`, which
# performs NO cryptographic verification: the maxima it reads are unverified at that point, so
# this is a SHAPE rule, not an authorization one. A row asserting it through a signed boundary
# would be proving a different -- stronger -- property than the one the code has.
#
# BOTH RUNTIMES compare these fields through their structural record boundary.
# Elixir RecordValidate.validate_bytes consumes the Go-authored record_boundary fixtures.
#
# WHAT IS EXCLUDED: whether a projected cost COVERS every real mutation is 1.5-k's. These rows
# verify only that a DECLARED cost does not exceed its capability-carried maxima.
#
# conjunct              relation  accepted            refused              go      elixir  owner
cost_model_version      equal     equal_to_claim      differs_from_claim   refuse  refuse  -
projected_row_count     at_most   equal_to_maximum    one_over_maximum     refuse  refuse  -
projected_write_bytes   at_most   equal_to_maximum    one_over_maximum     refuse  refuse  -
